title.narrative: Provision of immediate life-saving emergency food assistance through unconditional cash transfer to the drought-affected households in the Qansax Dheere district of the Bay Region.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe latest FSNU report directly indicates Nearly 4.6 million people in Somalia will likely experience high levels of acute food insecurity – IPC AFI Phase 3 or above (Crisis or worse) – between April and June 2025. This includes about 784,000 people (4 per cent of the population analysed) in IPC Phase 4 (Emergency) and nearly 3.8 million people (20 per cent of the population analysed) in IPC Phase 3 (Crisis). This reflects an increase compared to the projection done in January 2025, which estimated that 4.4 million people would be in IPC Phase 3 or above between April and June 2025. For the 21 areas analyzed as part of this update, the revised number of people in IPC Phase 3 or above between April and June 2025 is 713,000 people compared to 553,000 people estimated in the January 2025 analysis, or a net increase of nearly 160,000 people (29 cent). and Qasaxdheere is one of the districts that badly affected the changes of the humanitarian assistance and increased population displacement with a serous food insecurity and PDA grassroots coordination confirms the turnout of new displaced new arrivals joining the IDPs settlementsltbrgtIn response to the needs mentioned above, PDA process activities that are in line with the FSL cluster objectives. the project will contribute ltbrgtto the objectives of improving access to food by targeting nine locations of a total of 1630 HHs from (1) Aliyow Mad Araale rural 200 HHs, (2) Esow 100 HHs, (3) Raydabley rural 110 HHs, (4) Baadhaanto IDP 140 HHs, (5) Dhershenkuus IDP 350 HHs, (6) Diinsoor IDP 150 HHs, (7) Gadisow IDP 200 HHs, (8) October 100 HHs, and (9) Gobor Hoose IDP 200 HHs consisting of 52% Female and 48% male in Qansax Dheere district, and this is for host communities and and IDP ca Once the agreement is signed, PDA will conduct grassroots community consultation with community stakeholders. The community engagement will be inclusive, where all community stakeholders representing a variety of community groups, including women, people with disabilities (PWs), minority and marginalised communities, are involved. PDA’s community consultation is intended to provide the community the entire project information, such as project duration, project donor, criteria of beneficiary identification and registration, project targeting locations, beneficiary entitlement, and allocated households for each location, respectively, and from there the organisation will register 1630 vulnerable households with the help of the community leaders. The community engagement is intended for community ownership and community and promotes the accountability to the affected populations. The project addresses the need assessment conducted by PDA through community engagement, where we have noted that the population of Qansaxdheere district is completely food insecure and their first priority is to get unconditional cash transfers (UCT). PDA is implementing the food security project based on community needs which have been captured during PDA's community need assessment. ltbrgtThe PDA will provide the community the hotlines of both the SHF and PDA to improve community feedback, transparency and response effectiveness and efficiency these hotlines will be given to both targeting beneficiaries and community elders. During the community consultation, PDA will conduct humanitarian actor mapping in Qansax Dheere district, especially targeting to mitigate the risks of service duplication and promote project integration.
